questions.q: What did early nomadic people use the stars for?
a: Timing gatherings, harvests and animal migrations
Navigating across open oceans
Predicting earthquakes and floods
Measuring the distance to other stars
questions.why: Lesson 1 says nomads read the stars to set annual meeting times and know when fruit ripened or buffalo migrated.

questions.q: What did Copernicus argue, contrary to Ptolemy?
a: That the planets revolve around the sun
That the Earth sits at the center of everything
That planetary orbits are perfect circles
That gravity is a form of magnetism
questions.why: The summary says Ptolemy placed Earth at the center, and Copernicus later proposed that planets orbit the sun.

questions.q: How would aliens most likely make first contact, according to Sagan?
a: Through radio waves carrying a simple signal
By landing spacecraft in plain sight
By sending physical probes to Earth
By signaling with flashes of visible light
questions.why: Lesson 2 says radio is quick, cheap and simple, making it the most likely channel for a first message.

questions.q: Why would prime numbers make a good message from aliens?
a: They clearly show intention and intelligence
They are easy to translate into English
They describe the aliens' home planet
They require very advanced technology
questions.why: The summary says a set of prime numbers would communicate intention and intelligence succinctly and clearly.

questions.q: What do the Voyager probes carry for other civilizations?
a: Records of Earth's sounds, greetings and music
Maps showing the location of every country
Samples of soil and ocean water
A working model of the solar system
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes phonograph records holding greetings in many languages, favorite songs and natural sounds.
